subject: Replace Terminal Delight’s noisy Git ticker with window-wide coordination attention and a joined relationship inspector.
reader: Parker manages many agents, asked to remove the ticker, and is reviewing a revised UI plan after an independent browser review. He knows TD but should not need Rust knowledge.

sections.heading: Git Coordination
sections.text:
Your rail spends its top row on rotating Git facts. You asked to squash that ticker into nothing. Replace it with one window-wide attention signal, then open it when you need to inspect the connected work. 

 Revised proposal v2 · 4/10 About 6 minutes Native Rust / GPUI

sections.heading: The Glance
sections.text:
The closed signal covers projects in this window. Branch metrics and worktree inventory move into project inspection. Selecting a clear project leaves an alert elsewhere visible. 
 01 · A stable signal 

CURRENT · redrawn from your screenshot measured 

 1 WORKTREE · 1 SHARED ● ● ● ▰   1 lines of work, one shared · quiet for an hour 

PROPOSED · yellow = the amendments inferred 

 GIT ! ALERT 3 affected projects PARTIAL 
This window · detailed Git metrics are available on opening 

 NARROW · 320 CSS px 
 GIT ! ALERT 3 projects PARTIAL 

 One stable window-wide signal replaces the ticker. The proposed example has three affected projects while Client Portal is selected and clear. Quiet, complete observations reduce to a subdued GIT label. Current text is redrawn from your screenshot; all proposed counts and CSS widths are illustrative. 

Scope stays explicit: this TD window. Git attention remains separate from the agent-needs-input queue. Unknown and stale observations stay visible even when no overlap is currently established.

sections.heading: The Connection
sections.text:
Four worktrees touching one file share one hotspot . Work connected through shared files or checkouts forms a cluster , which can be inspected together. 
 02 · Count the shared place 

 The same checkout contributes once to file overlap. Its two panes also form a shared-checkout hotspot. This diagram follows the handoff’s grouping rule; it makes no claim that either pane authored a particular change. 

Today’s scanner compares branch pairs and omits untracked paths from overlap. Collect committed, staged, unstaged and untracked paths separately before building the groups.

 A clear selected project cannot hide an alert elsewhere. Expand Terminal Delight’s preview or open its project; select Shared host code for the joined relationship table. Toggle known identities to see B and C share one session. The dense fixture retains every hotspot behind bounded pages. All observations are fictional. 

 04 · Coverage survives the glance 

 ✓ CLEAR 0 observed groups Required observations complete 

 ▲ WARNING 2 observed groups Known-member paths complete · project graph incomplete 

 ? UNKNOWN Group count unknown Initial scan / unavailable

 Fewer observed groups can mean more connected work. A newly measured bridge joins the host and palette groups. Their count falls from two to one while warning remains. Known-member evidence and membership coverage travel separately in UI and MCP; a partial count is neither final nor a lower bound.

sections.heading: The Build
sections.text:
These views can share the scanner TD already runs in the background. Add the data in steps, derive connected groups once, and reuse that result for native rendering and permission-scoped MCP reads. 
 05 · Collect 

 Keep one Git worker. Extend its observations with source-labelled paths and stable checkout/pane identities. The legacy engineering report keeps its keys and meanings. Source: current scanner/cache seams plus proposed modules. 06 · Group 

 Derive connected work once per reading. Cache the graph and render it in the native overlay. No separate UI severity formula or scanner is needed. Source: current scanner/cache seams plus proposed modules. 07 · Expose 

 Apply permissions before deriving agent-visible groups. The MCP branch uses the same pure algorithm on authorized facts. Filtering a finished all-pane cluster would leak through its counts and paths. Source: current scanner/cache seams plus proposed modules. 

The existing two-second scheduling beat and twenty-second stale threshold are starting points. Each project retains its actual scan time; neither interval promises that every project is freshly measured. No Git subprocess runs during paint or an MCP request. 
 08 · Prove one route before expanding 

 1 
 Tracer: one shared checkout 
Stable pane/context identity → badge → project → evidence → focus, plus a permission-scoped MCP read of the same fixture. Keep unavailable fields visible. Pass: two panes become one shared-checkout hotspot; hidden panes change no visible aggregate. 

 2 
 Trustworthy file groups 
Collect four path sources with NUL-safe parsing; add multiway file hotspots and connected clusters. Preserve the legacy touched field. Pass: four worktrees sharing a file yield one hotspot; a bridge joins groups; a missing base qualifies committed overlap. 

 3 
 All projects and incremental reads 
Replace the ticker, rank projects and add preview children. Retain Checkouts, reconcile graph changes and ship the changes API. Push can wait. Pass: a clear selected project cannot conceal another project’s alert; unknown sorts ahead of clear; bridge lineage preserves the warning. 

 4 
 Native acceptance 
Exercise keyboard focus restoration, partial graphs, sparse and dense shared-file fixtures, privacy metadata, flat/warped hit testing and both supported core suites. Pass: no frame-time Git; bounded hotspot inspection; exact repeated-Escape sequence; one shared fixture drives native UI and actual MCP response tests. 

 The first slice proves the entire read-and-focus route. This changes the handoff’s ordering: privacy and MCP parity start with the tracer, before the full graph. No duration estimate is established.

sections.heading: The Decisions
sections.text:
Recommended: replace the ticker with one window-wide Git attention signal. Inspect projects, connected work and joined evidence through the existing collector and permission-scoped model. 

 Entry Point 
Replace the ticker. Summarize window-wide Git attention, expand project previews, and open project or cluster details. Preserve Git facts in inspection. 
Revised · a clear current project still exposes urgent Git attention elsewhere. 

 Signal Policy 
Show distinct labelled severity, the observed cause and comparable dimensions. Separate known-member evidence from project graph completeness; preserve unknown agent identity. 
Revised · stable severity ordering; partial group counts are provisional topology. 

 First Release 
Retain the collector, graph and permission-scoped MCP plan. Ship native views, reliable footprints and all four read/delta tools through the existing relay. Line analysis and push remain optional. 
Direction retained · preserve engineering_state compatibility and prove scoped native/MCP parity in the tracer.
